caveat: Complete memory against Context Runtime's selected memory (budget 3,000 tokens, context-runtime commit 3b55bec), 3 replicates per arm, one model. 2 of 3 selected replicates STOPPED with BudgetTooSmall after round 3 (they needed 3,030 and 3,035 tokens): a constant budget against a growing single-problem record ends this way by design, and that is the result. The one selected replicate that finished (target held-out 0.600) is inside the spread of the complete arm's three replicates (0.600, 0.967, 0.533), so there is no accuracy comparison and no equivalence or benefit claim. Selection cut the memory shown from 3,665-5,630 to 2,059-2,885 tokens and prompt tokens per engineer call by 33 percent, kept every attempt's measured fields (8 of 8), shortened every attempt description and dropped every rationale; it was not faster. Every record holds ONE problem, so relevance ranking and selection across problems were NOT exercised and are untested. The per-round 'history' values in results.json come from a faulty check and are not to be used; the corrected values are in history_recomputed_final_records.json.
reasons: two of three selected replicates stopped with BudgetTooSmall
one completed selected run cannot be compared with three noisy complete runs
every memory holds a single problem: selection among problems was not exercised
the budget was fixed in advance and not tuned
the first start of the run was interrupted and its output was not preserved
